title: Linking through unique student identifier
description: The student id submitted with the assignment is a unique identifier that can be used to link this submission data with other data about the same student across different systems or contexts.
assumptions: Student id is unique within the educational institution

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: The combination of student id, course, and submission timestamp can serve as quasi-identifiers that enable linking of this submission with other data points about the student.
assumptions: Course and timestamp combinations are sufficiently unique to identify individual students

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The Grades Portal explicitly processes identified data including student id, which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Student id is processed as part of the assignment submission workflow

title: Data contains unique identifier reference
description: The submission data contains a student id which is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject.
assumptions: Student id uniquely identifies each student in the system

title: Attributable submission data evidence
description: The assignment submission with student id, timestamp, and work file creates data that can be used to prevent the student from denying they submitted the assignment.
assumptions: Submission records are stored and can be retrieved as evidence

title: Metadata impacts deniability claims
description: Submission timestamp and file metadata can contain unintended data that impacts deniability claims about the assignment submission.
assumptions: File metadata and timestamps are captured during submission

title: Potentially sensitive work file data
description: The work file submitted may contain sensitive personal data beyond what is functionally required for grading purposes.
assumptions: Work files may contain personal information not necessary for assessment
uncertainty_note: Depends on the nature of assignments and what students include in their work

title: Implicit data disclosure through file metadata
description: File metadata (creation date, author, software used, etc.) may be implicitly collected as a side-effect of the explicit work file submission.
assumptions: File metadata is preserved during upload and storage

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of how their submission data (including metadata) is collected, processed, stored, or potentially disclosed beyond grading purposes.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Lack of student control over data processing preferences
description: Students may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their submission data is processed, stored, or shared beyond the immediate grading context.
assumptions: System may not provide granular consent options for data processing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Collecting and processing work files with embedded metadata may process more personal data than is actually needed for the functional goal of grading assignments.
assumptions: Some metadata in work files may not be necessary for grading
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data minimization practices of the institution

title: Linking through unique student identifier

title: Identifier in submission queue data
